title.value: Sparse Decomposition of Graph Neural Networks
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned as 'Sparse Decomposition of Graph Neural Networks' in the header of the paper.
title.quote: Sparse Decomposition of Graph Neural Networks

analysis.description: The paper addresses the high inference cost of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) due to large node aggregation. It proposes a sparse decomposition approach called SDGNN to efficiently approximate node representations using sparsely weighted sums of transformed features from selected subsets of nodes. This reduces complexity to be linear with average node degree and layers. The method is shown to improve inference speed and accuracy in tasks like node classification and spatio-temporal forecasting.

type.justification: The paper conducts extensive experiments demonstrating that their proposed method outperforms other models in terms of accuracy and speedup, indicating an empirical study.
type.quote: We demonstrate via extensive experiments that our method outperforms other baselines designed for inference speedup, achieving significant accuracy gains with comparable inference times

name.justification: The paper is centered around enhancing the efficiency of Graph Neural Network models through sparse decomposition techniques.
name.quote: Graph Neural Networks (GNN) exhibit superior performance in graph representation learning, but their inference cost can be high due to an aggregation operation.

name.justification: The study extensively experiments with node classification tasks, aiming to demonstrate the efficacy of their method in reducing inference time while maintaining accuracy.
name.quote: We validate SDGNN’s approximation power and inference efficiency through node classification tasks in the transductive setting.

name.justification: The method is applied in spatio-temporal forecasting tasks as part of the study, demonstrating its practical applications beyond node classification.
name.quote: We verify the approximation power of SDGNN and the scalability of our algorithm on seven node classification datasets and demonstrate how SDGNN can be effectively applied under the online prediction setting with two spatio-temporal forecasting datasets.
